Summary: The video features Phoebe, a UX designer at Khloe, who introduces the new features of the 7.0 release of the software. Below is a comprehensive guide based on the content of the transcript. **Introduction** - Phoebe welcomes viewers and introduces herself as a UX designer at Khloe. - She invites questions from the audience, which will be answered live. **Key Updates** 1. **Mac Equipment Improvements** - Enhanced performance for users on Mac computers with M1 silicon chips. - Commitment to ongoing optimization for better user experience. 2. **Pantone Integration** - Khloe now includes an updated Pantone color library accessible through the color window. - Users can search for colors by number or find similar colors. - Note on potential discrepancies with Pantone standards. 3. **Parametric Pattern Feature** - New feature allows users to create patterns without prior drafting knowledge. - Options for symmetry in pattern pieces are introduced. - Users can easily input measurements for front and back patterns, including sleeves. 4. **Grading Tools Updates** - Improved ease of use for grading tools, including dropdown selections for sizes. - Introduction of guides for precision adjustments. - Enhanced functionalities for right-click options and precision boxes. 5. **DXF Import Enhancements** - New options for rotating grain lines during DXF import. - Help to resolve previous issues with grain line alignment. 6. **Exporting and Importing Files** - Ability to export rule files and import CSV files into the POM tab for easier management of POMs and PLMs. - New drag-and-drop functionality for adding fabrics in the colorway editor. 7. **2D Pattern Improvements** - Smart guides for adding points and split lines. - Flattening tool optimizations for better performance and accuracy in creating patterns. 8. **Schematic Render Improvements** - Visibility of button outlines in the schematic render window and options for customizing thread lines. 9. **3D Features Enhancements** - Ability to move the avatar and garment together in the 3D space. - Adjustments to 3D background images and colorway mode, including the ability to hide/show graphics. 10. **BOM and Nesting Improvements** - BOM is relocated to the editor toolbar for easier access. - Real-time updates for nesting results. 11. **Emulator Mode Updates** - Adjustments to stretch force tolerance for high-stretch fabrics. 12. **Zipper and Binding Tool Updates** - Separate adjustments for zipper teeth and tape. - New binding options that allow for binding on both sides of fabric and on seam lines. 13. **Trim and Button Enhancements** - Convert patterns to trims and duplicate trims to symmetric patterns. - Ability to add buttons to internal lines. 14. **Color Switch in Texture Editor** - Allows for color editing of individual colors within prints and graphics. 15. **Library and Object Browser Structure** - Introduction of a tree structure for better navigation in the library and object browser. 16. **Fur Length Update** - Maximum fur length increased to 1000 millimeters, allowing for more extensive fur designs. 17. **Community Engagement** - Announcement of the official Khloe Discord server for user interaction, sharing tips, and accessing news. **Conclusion** - Phoebe expresses excitement about the new features and encourages users to provide feedback. - She thanks viewers for watching and invites them to like and subscribe for more tips and tricks.

Each function serves a distinct purpose, and understanding how to use them effectively can enhance the garment creation process. **Strengthen Function:** - Purpose: Used to temporarily stiffen a garment, helping to correct issues like twisted fabric or improper drape. - How to Use: 1. Right-click on the pattern piece in either the 2D or 3D window. 2. Select the "strengthen" option from the context menu. 3. The selected piece will turn orange, indicating that the strengthen function is activated. 4. Start the simulation; the fabric will become stiffer, allowing the garment to regain its intended shape. - To revert the effect: - Repeat the initial steps or use the shortcut Ctrl + H on a PC. - Simulate again for a more natural drape. - Note: This function is meant for temporary use. **Solidify Function:** - Purpose: Unlike strengthen, solidify maintains the desired drape or fold of a garment without altering its visual appearance. - How to Use: 1. After achieving the desired drape on the garment (e.g., rolled-up sleeves), use solidify to keep that shape intact. 2. This function allows the garment to retain its drape while still being manipulable during simulation. - Comparison with Strengthen: - If strengthen is applied, the fabric becomes stiffer and may alter the drape, whereas solidify preserves the drape. - Application Methods: - Right-click on the pattern piece to find the solidify option. - Alternatively, use the property editor to turn it on. **Bound Function:** - Purpose: Similar to interfacing in physical garment construction, the bound function provides structure to specific areas such as collars, cuffs, and small pieces. - How to Use: 1. Select the piece you wish to apply bound to and locate it in the property editor. 2. Activate the bound function by ticking the appropriate box. 3. Choose a preset that best fits the garment's needs. - Alternative Application: - If you want to apply bound to only part of the pattern, create an internal shape using the internal line polygon tool. - Draw the shape starting from inside the pattern, ensuring to close the shape. - Select the created shape, then activate the bound function in the property editor.
